what_happened: iMessage liaison Monitor on Mac Studio went through five iterations before stabilizing. Each version had a different bug: (1) IFS=tab read split multi-line bodies on newlines, generating dozens of malformed events per long inbound and saturating the notification stream so subsequent inbounds went unsurfaced; (2) SQL-side NOT EXISTS suppression of is_from_me=0 rows whose body matched a recent is_from_me=1 row — broken because Tony iPhone and Mac Studio share Apple ID E:[email-redacted], so iCloud writes both is_from_me=1 (account sent) and is_from_me=0 (this device received) for every Tony send too, not just for assistant outbounds; (3) shell-side outbox file with grep -Fxq exact-match — broken because plugin appends signature "Sent by Claude" to outbounds; (4) signature-strip added but echo $REPLY wrote multi-line replies as multiple outbox lines while SQL flattened body to one line, so multi-line outbounds never matched; (5) flatten-on-write fixed that, but SQL substr(...,1,200) truncated the body to 200 chars while outbox stored full body, so long outbounds couldn t exact-match. Final fix: prefix-match via awk index($0,p)==1 instead of grep -Fxq. Five commits, one stable Monitor.
what_learned: Three reusable principles for chat-database listeners on a shared-Apple-ID Mac. (a) chat.db has no column distinguishing this Mac sent it from another device on the same Apple ID sent it (message_source, share_direction, account, destination_caller_id are all identical) — SQL-side suppression cannot disambiguate; you must track outbounds out-of-band via a sentinel file written by the sending session. (b) Always normalize both sides of any text comparison: same newline handling (collapse char(10) to space), same length (prefix-match if one side is truncated), same suffix handling (strip plugin signature). The bash-pipe-to-SQL flow is full of representation drift; one mismatch breaks the filter silently. (c) Multi-line bash echo to a file appends multiple lines, not one; use printf with tr to flatten. The Monitor pattern is now persisted in ~/.claude/projects/-Users-tony-studio/memory/imessage_listen.md with the final query, the reply discipline, and the four bug postmortems.
